clue.text: Protector for the club team?

parts.note: an iron is a golf club
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A question about who guards the golf club's team.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lord Protector, Oliver Cromwell, was nicknamed 'Old Ironsides', and his cavalry were the Ironsides.
explanation.definitionFit: A nickname of Cromwell, England's Lord Protector, so the historical title stands for him.

clue.text: Where to do one's civic duty, but it hurts

definitions.text: Where to do one's civic duty
definitions.meaning: serving on a jury is a citizen's duty, so you do it sitting in a jury
a wound or harm is something that hurts

explanation.surface: Jury service is a public duty, but a painful one.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is where jurors serve; as one word it is damage that causes pain.

clue.text: Unclear work on a question on English

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Some work on an English question is hard to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaque writing is obscure, impossible to see through, hence unclear.

clue.text: Fragment caught in a moment of delicacy

indicators.note: the fragment and catch are placed inside the moment

parts.note: a shake is a moment, as in 'in two shakes'
an ort is a scrap or fragment of food
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A small piece is captured in a delicate moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet biscuity cake is a treat, a dainty item of food.

clue.text: Sweet to make love with one from the canteen

parts.note: a sweet is a dessert, the pudding course
to spoon is an old word for kiss and cuddle

explanation.surface: Someone is sweetly courting, with cutlery involved.
explanation.walkthrough: A canteen here is a boxed set of cutlery, not a works cafeteria.
explanation.definitionFit: A canteen of cutlery holds sets of spoons, so this is one item from the box.

clue.text: Angry old man returning to part of the Hebrides

indicators.note: returning means the word for the angry address is read backwards

parts.note: sirrah is an old form of address to a man, used in anger or contempt

explanation.surface: A cross old fellow goes back home to a Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: Harris is the southern part of the island of Lewis and Harris in the Outer Hebrides.

clue.text: Street map with river shown in colour

parts.note: an A-Z is a book of street maps of a city
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A street map marks a river in a colour.
explanation.walkthrough: An A to Z is the standard British city street atlas.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright sky blue is a colour, from heraldry and poetry.

clue.text: Repeat animation amazingly ran a week

indicators.note: amazingly suggests the letters of 'ran a week' are thrown about

explanation.surface: A rerun of a cartoon surprisingly lasts a week.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to life again is to be roused anew, a second bout of animation.

clue.text: Ask one's mum about being a bit thick

indicators.note: the word for mum goes around the other pieces

parts.note: sh is a call for silence; to keep mum is to be quiet
to tout is to solicit, ask for custom
one's read as 'one is' gives I and IS

explanation.surface: Someone asks their mother about seeming slow-witted.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoutish means somewhat stout, that is fairly thick or plump.

clue.text: Crawling after girl almost caused Othello's downfall

indicators.note: after puts the crawling word behind the girl
almost means the girl's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Jean is a girl's name
lousy means crawling with lice

explanation.surface: Grovelling after a girl nearly brought down Othello.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's play Othello is destroyed by envy of his wife's supposed lover.

clue.text: Right shaky about distorted rhythm

indicators.note: shaky suggests the letters of 'about' are unsteady and jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone's correct but nervous about a warped beat.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubato is musical tempo stretched and squeezed expressively, a distortion of strict time.

clue.text: Dash to work and hope for an election

definitions.meaning: literally to hurry to one's office
to stand as a candidate for public post

explanation.surface: A commuter's dash doubles as a political campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a sprint to the workplace; idiomatically to stand as a candidate.

clue.text: Writer heading off to cause stir

indicators.note: heading off means the writer's name loses its first letter

parts.note: Marcel Proust was a French novelist

explanation.surface: An author leaves to make a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: To roust is to rouse or stir someone out of bed or into action.

clue.text: Passed over German worker in high spirits

parts.note: ex means former, past
uber is German for over
an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: A German employee was passed over for promotion but stays cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: Exuberant means full of energy and excitement, lively and cheerful.

clue.text: Fun itself has to be sacrificed to loyalty

indicators.note: sacrificed suggests the phrase 'Fun itself has' is broken up and remade

explanation.surface: Enjoyment must be given up for the sake of devotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Faithfulness is steadfast allegiance, the same quality as loyalty.

clue.text: Creature at the core is the bravest

parts.note: a lion is a creature
the heart is the core of something

explanation.surface: An animal with courage at its centre is the boldest.
explanation.definitionFit: A lionheart is a very courageous person, like Richard I.

clue.text: Growth in imitation stone

parts.note: a sham is a fake, an imitation
rock is stone

explanation.surface: Something grows in fake stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A shamrock is a clover-like plant, something that grows.

clue.text: Diverted into side issues

indicators.note: diverted suggests the letters of 'into side' are sent off course

explanation.surface: Someone is distracted into minor matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Editions of a newspaper or magazine are its issues.

clue.text: Prevaricate, argue, quarrel — it's such a little thing

parts.note: to hedge is to avoid committing oneself
to spar is to argue
a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: Evading, arguing, fighting: all over something trivial.
explanation.definitionFit: The dunnock is a small brown songbird, a little creature of hedgerows.

clue.text: Eliza Doolittle's refuge, a bower

indicators.note: Eliza Doolittle, the Cockney flower girl of Pygmalion, drops her aitches

parts.note: a harbour is a refuge or shelter

explanation.surface: The heroine of My Fair Lady has a leafy hideaway.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbour is a shady garden shelter of trees or climbers, the same as a bower.

clue.text: The endless story's a yarn

indicators.note: endless means the word 'The' loses its last letter

parts.note: a story is a read, as in 'a good read'

explanation.surface: The tale goes on forever: a real yarn.
explanation.definitionFit: A yarn is a spun thread, not a tale, in this sense.

clue.text: Take precaution against possible attackers

parts.note: sounds like home security, but the attackers are fabric-eating insects in a wardrobe

explanation.definitionFit: To protect clothes from moths, insects whose larvae chew wool, with treatment or repellent.

clue.text: Head grasps the point: make it stick

indicators.note: grasps means the head holds the point inside it

parts.note: the pate is the head
S is south, a compass point

explanation.surface: Someone finally understands the point and makes it memorable.
explanation.definitionFit: To paste is to glue, fixing one thing so it sticks to another.

clue.text: Redhead, into pot, becomes strident

indicators.note: into puts the first letter of 'Red' inside the pot

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis, also called hash

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the word 'Red'

explanation.surface: A ginger person who takes drugs becomes loud.
explanation.definitionFit: A harsh sound is grating and strident.

clue.text: Player starts to open, bowling overs in second test

indicators.note: starts means the first letters of the following six words

explanation.surface: A cricket commentary about opening the bowling in a second Test.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket words mislead: the player is a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboist plays the oboe, so is a musical player.

clue.text: Clothing found in heap in a forest

indicators.note: found in signals the letters sit inside 'heap in a forest'

explanation.surface: Garments discovered in a pile in the woods.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinafore is an apron or sleeveless dress, an item of clothing.

clue.text: A thousand items delivered — and that's your lot!

parts.note: K stands for a thousand

indicators.note: delivered suggests the letters of 'items' are shifted about

explanation.surface: A thousand goods are delivered, and that's all you're getting.
explanation.definitionFit: Kismet is fate, one's lot in life.

clue.text: Dared to let rip about return game

indicators.note: about means the venting word goes around the other piece

parts.note: vented means let rip, expressed anger freely

indicators.note: return means the abbreviation for the game is read backwards

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game

explanation.surface: Someone dared to let fly over a return match.
explanation.definitionFit: Ventured means risked or dared to do something.
